newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish secularists close to coalition agreement.
newsitem.headline: Turkish secularists close to coalition agreement.

text.p: Three secularist Turkish parties were close to agreement on a protocol outlining the policies of a planned anti-Islamist coalition and the distribution of cabinet seats, Anatolian news agency said.
The agency said the parties would ask President Suleyman Demirel to approve the government, led by Mesut Yilmaz, within a few days.
"Work on the government programme will be completed on Monday, or Tuesday at the latest," Anatolian said.
Two more MPs have resigned from the ruling pro-Islamist alliance, further boosting Mesut Yilmaz's hopes of winning a confidence vote for his secularist partnership.
"We haven't been able to secure stability in parliament. That is why I have made this move, aimed at uniting the right," Anatolian quoted deputy Evren Bulut as saying on Saturday night.
Another True Path deputy, Ali Gunaydin, quit the party on Sunday, the agency said. Both were expected to back Yilmaz at the confidence vote, due within two weeks.
Yilmaz now has 277 votes on paper, compared to True Path and the Islamists who can command the support of 270 MPs.
His coalition is expected to give priority to encouraging secularist education and changing the electoral laws before early elections by next spring at the latest.
He was asked by the president to find a new government after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, resigned earlier this month.
